- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% based on sentiment decay.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to reflect mean reversion toward historical mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model typically underreacts to sentiment shifts; delay correction by 1–3 days if sentiment turns positive.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
- Avoid over-relying on recent 3–5 day highs; if sentiment is bullish but price is falling, model may misread trend; apply cautionary downward bias.
